feedback: This candidate keeps the same geometry and sensor layout as before, which has proven stable and well balanced. The controller parameters have been further softened compared to iteration 1: base_speed is reduced to 0.9, kp to 5, kd to 1.5, and ki increased to 1.5. This follows the evidence from iteration 1 where the robot performed well on oval and s-bend tracks but failed the slalom due to excessive speed and steering oscillation. The reduced base_speed and softer PID gains should help reduce overshoot and oscillations in tight curves, improving slalom completion. The increased integral gain aims to enhance steady-state error correction, potentially lowering rms error on curves. The sensor weights and line loss strategy remain unchanged, as they have provided good line detection and recovery. Depending on the next race results, if the robot still fails to complete the slalom or shows high steering oscillation, consider further reducing base_speed or tuning PID gains. If the robot completes with high rms error, try adjusting sensor weights or increasing ki further. Overall, this candidate is a reasonable step to improve slalom performance by prioritizing stability and precision over speed.
requested_changes: controller.base_speed: 0.8 if slalom completion still fails (iteration 1 evidence)
controller.kp: 4 and controller.kd: 1 if steering oscillation remains high (iteration 1 evidence)
controller.ki: 2.0 if rms_error remains high on curves (iteration 1 evidence)
